summary: An 80-ft Aermotor MC-39 steel tower on the White Mountain Apache Reservation, built in 1934 to replace a 1925 tower; the register lists it in active service.

facts.design: 80-ft steel tower with 7 x 7 ft cab (Aermotor MC-39), built 1934 to replace a 60-ft tower from 1925

access.note: On the White Mountain Apache Reservation. A travel site says a recreation permit from the tribal Game and Fish department is required, invites readers to climb to the top, and says access to the tower varies; confirm current rules with the tribe.

events.note: 80-ft steel tower with 7 x 7 ft cab replaced the 1925 tower; the register says it was one of three Aermotor MC-39 towers installed on the reservation that year
Registered January 31, 2002; nominated by Dave Lorenz, AZ/NM Registrar

evidence.supports: lookout continues in active service; one of three Aermotor MC-39 towers installed in 1934 on the reservation
evidence.quote: One of three Aermotor MC-39 towers installed in 1934 on the White Mountain Apache Indian Reservation, Maverick Mountain Lookout continues in active service.

evidence.supports: 80-ft steel tower with 7 x 7 ft cab replaced a 60-ft tower built on the site in 1925
evidence.quote: The 80' steel tower with 7' x 7' cab replaced a similar but shorter (60') tower built on the site in 1925.

evidence.supports: administered by the White Mountain Apache Agency
registered January 31, 2002; nominated by Dave Lorenz, AZ/NM Registrar
location on the White Mountain Apache Reservation in Apache County

evidence.quote: You're driving on sovereign tribal land, and rolling through without permission is trespassing.

evidence.supports: travel site calls the 1934 tower a 60-foot steel structure
evidence.quote: This impressive 60-foot steel structure has been keeping watch over the Apache forests for nearly a century.

evidence.supports: recreation permit from the Tribal Game and Fish department is required
evidence.quote: grab a recreation permit from the Tribal Game and Fish department—it's non-negotiable.
Fair warning: this road is completely unpaved.

evidence.quote: Climb to the top and you'll be rewarded with jaw-dropping views

evidence.supports: travel site says access to the tower itself varies
evidence.quote: Just know that access to the tower itself varies

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not fully resolved. The register gives the 1934 tower as 80 ft and the 1925 tower as 60 ft; the travel site calls the 1934 tower 60 ft. The register is the primary source and is used for the story; the travel site is noted as disagreeing.

sources.title: Maverick Mountain: Driving to the 8,086ft lookout in Fort Apache

notes_for_editor: Record access was 'unknown'; now 'permission' based only on a travel site (RoadScout), not an official source. Confirm the permit rule with the White Mountain Apache Tribe before relying on it. Staffing and fire history were not found in any source read. The register's 'continues in active service' is undated. Height conflict: register gives 80 ft for the 1934 tower, RoadScout gives 60 ft. An FFLA Facebook repost of the register text appeared only in search results and was not used. RoadScout says 'Climb to the top' and that access to the tower varies; the story advises against climbing because no official source gives a climbing rule. The story previously said no source mentioned climbing; that was wrong and is corrected.
